cards.text: Proverbs 27 is a box of short sayings from Solomon, king of Israel, copied by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah (Proverbs 25:1). There's no plot here, friend, just one bite of wisdom after another. And the very first bite is about tomorrow.

cards.question: Solomon says don't boast about tomorrow. Why not?

answers.text: You do not know what a day may bring
Your neighbor will hold it against you
Your words will fall back on your head

cards.text: One night I'm lying in the back of a junk drawer, and the next thing I know I'm on a COOKIE PLANET, so no, friend, I do not know what a day may bring (27:1). Next, Solomon talks about praise, and whose mouth it should come from.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the best praise comes from your own mouth.

cards.text: Let somebody else praise you, even a stranger, and not your own lips (27:2). So I guess I have to stop calling myself WORLD FAMOUS, friend, when nobody outside this bakery has ever heard of me.

cards.question: Solomon says a stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but the aggravation from a ___ outweighs them both.

cards.text: Then Solomon lines up some strong feelings. Wrath is cruel, and anger is like a flood (27:4).

cards.question: After wrath and anger, Solomon names one more feeling and asks who can withstand it. Which one?

cards.text: Who can withstand jealousy? Then Solomon says, "Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed."

cards.question: Solomon says the wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are ___.
Solomon brings up honey. Which soul does he say loathes it?
True or false: Solomon says that to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
Solomon paints a picture of a man who wanders from his home. What does he say that man is like?

answers.text: A bird that strays from its nest
A sheep that strays from its flock
A ship that drifts from its harbor

cards.text: More from Solomon's box of sayings. Oil and incense bring joy to the heart (27:9).

cards.question: Solomon says oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a ___ is sweetness to the soul.

cards.text: Then: don't forsake your friend, or your father's friend. And in your day of calamity, don't go to your brother's house (27:10).

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says a neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away.

cards.text: When your car dies at two in the morning, your brother three states over sends a sad face, and your neighbor shows up in slippers with jumper cables. Then the voice turns to speak to "my son" (27:11).

cards.question: The speaker asks his son to be wise and bring joy to his heart. What does the speaker say that will let the speaker himself do?

answers.text: Answer the one who taunts him
Rest easy in his old age
Pass on his land in peace

cards.text: Next up, Solomon puts two kinds of people in front of the same danger: the prudent and the simple. Friend, they do NOT end up in the same place.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the simple see danger and take cover.

cards.text: It's the prudent who see danger and take cover. The simple keep going and pay the penalty, like a driver who sees BRIDGE OUT and figures it's out for OTHER people (27:12).

cards.question: Solomon gives advice about a man who posts security for a stranger. What does he say to take from him?

cards.text: And if the security is for a foreigner, Solomon says to get collateral (27:13).

cards.question: Solomon says blessing your neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning will be counted as a ___.

cards.text: Friend, a blessing at full volume at five in the morning is just an alarm clock with good intentions. Next, Solomon says a constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike (27:15).

cards.question: Solomon says restraining a contentious woman is like grasping oil with one's right hand. What else does he say it's like?

cards.text: Now Solomon pictures iron against iron, and friend, this one's a keeper (27:17).

cards.question: Solomon pictures iron against iron. What does he say one man does to another, the same way?

cards.text: Friend, I spent years with soft edges in the back of a junk drawer, so I KNOW how good sharp feels. Then Solomon says whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit (27:18).

cards.question: Solomon says whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever looks after his ___ will be ___.
Solomon says that as water reflects the face, something else reflects the true man. What is it?

cards.text: Next, Solomon says Sheol, the realm of the dead, and Abaddon, a word for destruction, are never satisfied (27:20).

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says that, like Sheol and Abaddon, the eyes of man are never satisfied.

cards.text: Ever say "just one more video" at eleven at night and look up at two in the morning? Then Solomon turns to metal: a crucible for silver and a furnace for gold (27:21).

cards.question: Solomon says silver is tested in a crucible and gold in a furnace. What does he say tests a man?

cards.text: One nice word about my sprinkles and I'm strutting around this bakery like I invented the cookie. Then Solomon paints a picture with a mortar and a pestle (27:22).

cards.question: Solomon pictures grinding a fool like grain with a mortar and pestle. What does he say happens to the fool's folly?

answers.text: It will not depart from him
It is crushed away for good

cards.text: Now Solomon wraps up with some farm advice. Know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds (27:23).

cards.question: Why does Solomon say to keep a close eye on your flocks and herds?

cards.text: Not even a crown endures to every generation (27:24). Then the hay is removed, new growth appears, and the grass from the hills is gathered (27:25).

cards.question: Once the grass is gathered, Solomon says the lambs will provide you with ___, and the goats with the price of a field.
True or false: Solomon says the goats' milk will feed you, but not your household.

cards.text: Plenty of goats' milk, food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants (27:27). Look after the flock and the flock looks after you, which is EXACTLY the deal I have with my ovens.
